topIssues.title: Alpha design and branding
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
Apply Alpha Compute’s design and branding to the finished phone experience.

## Detailed Description

**Estimate:** 5 working days, October 6–12. **After:** https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/31025 and all preceding project work.

- Agree the Alpha Compute logo, colors, typography and key screen designs.
- Apply the approved design to onboarding, chat/voice, settings, pairing and phone screens.
- Update app name, icons, splash/boot branding and other visible product identity. Preserve required license notices.
- Keep package identity, signing, authentication and update compatibility intact; coordinate any required identity changes across app and AOSP.
- Install the branded release on all four phones and recheck pairing, voice, Blooio SMS, calls and restart/reconnect.
- Hand over the design assets and repeatable white-label build configuration.

- Keep Alpha trademarks and brand assets out of public releases; deliver reusable design/build changes upstream and Alpha assets through the private handoff.
- Complete final source/build handoff and agreed P0/P1 checks on the branded release. Nubs owns the three-minute recording in #31025. Provide the stakeholder demo and one follow-up Q&A; track client review separately from implementation dates.

**Done when:** Alpha reviews the branded screens and all four phones run the approved branded release without regressions.

topIssues.title: ci(cloud-stability): deterministic-keyless lane red on develop since grounded reminder delivery stopped consuming the dispatch fixtures
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
## Summary

The `Validate develop` workflow is red at the current tip `4573712ebf` because the `cloud / agent-stability / deterministic-keyless` lane fails on every attempt, and `Complete manifest` fails with it ("Require one current green row per surface").

Run: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/36636159978 (2026-09-29T21:52Z). The previous run at `2a464d8413` (https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/36628914261) was green; the two runs in between were cancelled by later pushes, so this is the first observed run after the reminder-delivery change landed.

## Failure

The step summary only prints `{"status":"failed","firstAttemptPassed":false,"passedAttempts":0}`. The uploaded `cloud-stability-keyless-1` artifact carries the reason in each attempt's `scenario.stdout.log` (identical for attempts 01-03):

```text
| cloud-stability-agent | failed | 1470ms | deterministic model fixtures were not consumed:
[{"name":"cloud-reminder-dispatch-body","consumed":0,"min":1,"max":1,"required":true},
 {"name":"cloud-reminder-dispatch-title","consumed":0,"min":1,"max":1,"required":true}] |
```

The reminder itself was created and dispatched: the scenario's `assertCloudReadback` guard was never reached because the fixture-consumption check fails first, and the `scenario-report.json` shows `OWNER_REMINDERS_CREATE` with `cadence.kind: "once"`, `metadata.ownerSurface: "OWNER_REMINDERS"`, one `in_app` plan step.

## Cause

`packages/cloud/e2e/scenarios/cloud-stability-agent.scenario.ts` declares two required `TEXT_SMALL` fixtures for the dispatch path:

- `cloud-reminder-dispatch-body` (matches `Current reminder:\n- title: Review the synthetic Cloud inbox`, cardinality 1)
- `cloud-reminder-dispatch-title` (matches `Message body:\nTime to review the synthetic Cloud inbox.`, cardinality 1)

Since `51bd56787c` (fix(reminders): deliver grounded one-shot content without prose rewriting, via #32931 merged as `6d13e67446`), `RemindersService` no longer calls the model for exactly this reminder shape. In `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/lifeops/domains/reminders-service.ts` the `exactReminder` branch (owner occurrence, `in_app`, lifecycle `plan`, `cadence.kind === "once"`, `metadata.ownerSurface === "OWNER_REMINDERS"`, no `bodyOverride`) builds the body with `buildReminderBody` (`Reminder: <title>\nDue: <local time>`) and issues a `ReminderPresentation` whose title is the literal `Reminder`; `renderReminderBody` and `renderOwnerNotificationTitle` are only reached on the non-exact path. The scenario's reminder satisfies every `exactReminder` condition, so neither `TEXT_SMALL` call happens and the two required fixtures stay at `consumed: 0`.

The readback assertion itself still holds with the grounded body (`notification.body.includes("synthetic Cloud inbox")` matches `Reminder: Review the synthetic Cloud inbox`).

## Fix

Remove the two dead fixtures from the deterministic scenario (they encode the pre-`51bd56787c` prose-rewriting contract), leaving the readback assertion to pin the grounded dispatch. Only the deterministic lane is affected; `stability:real` uses the same scenario without fixtures.

I am opening a PR for this.

topIssues.title: gateway-webhook cutover hold: a turn settled while another replica held the lease is redelivered once that lease lapses
topIssues.author: nothingxnowhere
topIssues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`drainCutoverHolds` (`packages/cloud/services/gateway-webhook/src/cutover-hold.ts`) fences record removal to the current lease owner: the Lua step at `:255-258` refuses to delete the hold record when a *different* token owns the lease. That fence is correct while the other owner is alive. It leaves a gap when the other owner dies:

1. Drainer A acquires the lease and starts redelivering a held Blooio or Twilio turn.
2. A's renewal fails for a whole lease period, the lease lapses, and replica B acquires it (`set nx`). B then dies before draining.
3. A's turn completes. The dedup ledger is written `delivered`, but A's `removeHeldRecord()` returns 0 because B's token owns the lease, so the record and its index entry stay.
4. B's lease lapses. The next drainer acquires the lease, finds a live record, and calls `redeliver` without looking at the ledger. The Cloud turn runs again and the provider receives a second send.

This is the "P2" probe from the review of #32909 and the case #32944 left out of scope. #32944 fixed the sibling case where the lease lapsed with *no* new owner; this one needs the drainer to notice that the ledger has already left `held`.

**To Reproduce**

The real `handleWebhook` and `drainCutoverHolds` against the local `Bun.serve` Cloud stub and in-memory Redis used by `__tests__/cutover-hold.test.ts` (Bun 1.3.14, Node 24.15.0, `--conditions=eliza-source`). A signed Blooio webhook is held during a `503 personal_cutover_in_progress`. Cloud is then attested, and while the attested turn runs the lease key is overwritten with another replica's token. After the first drain the lease is deleted (the other replica died and its lease lapsed) and a second drain runs.

On `190d8a3304` (#32944's head) the second drain redelivers:

```
$ bun test --conditions=eliza-source __tests__/cutover-hold.test.ts -t "another replica owned the lease"
534 |     expect(second).toEqual({
error: expect(received).toEqual(expected)
-   "delivered": 0,
+   "delivered": 1,
(fail) connector ingress during Shared→Dedicated cutover > a hold settled while another replica owned the lease is not redelivered once that lease lapses
 0 pass
 1 fail
```

Gateway log for the message (timestamps and trace ids omitted): the turn completes twice and the provider egress runs twice.

```
{"level":"warn","message":"Personal connector turn held for Dedicated cutover","platform":"blooio","messageId":"msg_cutover_8","holdCode":"personal_cutover_in_progress"}
{"level":"info","message":"Personal Eliza connector message completed","platform":"blooio","messageId":"msg_cutover_8","cloudAttempts":1,"egressMs":2,"totalMs":3}
{"level":"info","message":"Held personal connector turn delivered after cutover","platform":"blooio","messageId":"msg_cutover_8","attempts":1}
{"level":"info","message":"Personal Eliza connector message completed","platform":"blooio","messageId":"msg_cutover_8","cloudAttempts":1,"egressMs":1,"totalMs":4}
```

**Expected behavior**

A drainer that acquires the lease over a record whose dedup ledger is no longer `held` does not redeliver. It removes the record under the same owner fence and moves on. The turn above runs once and the provider receives one send.

**Screenshots / recording of the wrong behavior (required for anything visible)**

N/A - server-side gateway queue behaviour with no rendered surface; the test transcript and gateway log above are the proof.

**Evidence / reproduction proof**

- [x] MP4 recording or JPG screenshots of the broken behavior: N/A - no visible surface; see the transcript.
- [x] Backend logs and frontend console/network logs when relevant: gateway log above; N/A for frontend (no UI).
- [x] Real-LLM trajectory when the bug involves agent/action/prompt/model behavior: N/A - no model call; the Cloud route is a local stub.
- [x] Domain artifacts when relevant: the drain statistics and the `delivered` ledger with a surviving record, in the transcript.

**Additional context**

The remaining unguarded window is two live drainers running the same turn concurrently, which happens only if renewal fails and a second replica acquires the lease while the first turn is still in flight. Lease renewal (`renewLeaseWhileRedelivering`) exists to prevent that, and the ledger check below cannot see it because the ledger stays `held` until a turn settles.

**Contribution provenance**

topPRs.title: Add durable approved workflows and device actions with managed Cloud identity
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Agent clients need durable, owner-bound workflows and reviewed device operations that survive interruptions, reconnects and process restarts. This change adds generic runtime contracts and persistence for those flows, including managed Cloud Google delegation, hosted results and selected Maps reads.

- Durable workflow authoring, validation, approval receipts, lifecycle changes and hosted delivery retain explicit approval and owner boundaries. Generic approval presentation is authoritative; legacy metadata remains a compatibility reader with downgrade rejection.
- Device actions bind proposals, approval, claim and immutable receipts to authenticated owner, agent and device enrollment. Selected Maps reads require negotiated capability and matching target identity; replay retrieves the bounded historical result without a new device read.
- Managed Cloud owner configuration and Google delegation provide identity and Gmail/Calendar access boundaries with server-side credentials and scope checks.
- Action discovery retains umbrella actions when a resource-specific alias matches, preserving role and context eligibility.
- Workflow mutation replies carry canonical receipts from the actual committed definition. Cancellation provenance is captured under the row lock, with per-service workflow control serialization. Submission, cancellation requests and pending device approvals cannot serve as proof that the requested operation completed. Pending workflow widgets retain their callback delivery.

Validation at prior head 252152eaa0352fd26f4824371e967bbf4e828bfd:

- Focused workflow SQL/worker/settlement/evaluator/parser checks: 7 tests and 243 assertions passed; workflow typecheck and lint passed.
- Device HTTP/PGlite lifecycle and evaluator checks passed, including refusal of false completion claims for pending approval, unknown outcomes and selected reads; assistant and agent typechecks passed.
- Independent source review found no remaining blocker in the receipt correction. Cancellation serialization is per service instance; it is not a cross-process SQLite guarantee.
- Full frozen installation, all284 standard root tasks and audits, emitted host build, twelve compiler cases, packaged Reminder flow and import guard passed with unchanged source. The original aggregate run failed on an unexplained cancellation HTTP reset. Separate unchanged-source workflow recovery passed31/31 files and167 tests; that original failure remains recorded.
- The separately enabled historical compiler-upgrade E2E passed24 assertions with historical source and current dependencies.
- Actual Cerebras qwen-3.8-27b chat completed with seven model calls, created one inactive unscheduled workflow, then a manually reviewed source was explicitly approved and executed once to return56. Removal preserved canonical approval/execution/lifecycle receipts, confirmed by fresh readback. This is local synthetic workflow acceptance.

Hosted CI36908850398 completed successfully at exact head252152eaa0352fd26f4824371e967bbf4e828bfd, including source/build checks, billing replay and PostgreSQL.

Native paired Maps flows, Cloud login/Gmail revocation and physical-device acceptance remain pending. This draft does not establish complete MVP or deployment acceptance.

Current head ab8f9a7110ae adds one bounded correction for model-authored invalid source quotes before any response field or action effects. The exact source validator remains unchanged; a repeated invalid reply fails closed. Actual HTTP/auth/PGlite/planner tests pass four cases, including one pending Maps proposal with rejected draft facts absent from storage. Sixteen owning pipeline cases, production and test-inclusive typechecks and formatting checks pass. Full exact-head qualification and live provider/native acceptance are pending.

topPRs.title: Harden action admission, confidential host boundaries, and privacy controls
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body: ## Summary This PR implements the code findings from the compliance research review (`compliance-research-2026-09-18`) across core, agent, cloud and app/ui, re-checked against HEAD. It also removes about 2,500 lines of dead or duplicate code. ### core - A typed modality table drives PII swap and binary/text handling. `TEXT_EMBEDDING_BATCH`, `TEXT_TO_SPEECH` and `PII_SCRUB` are no longer pseudonymized. - A host-only processing policy extends `ConfidentialInferenceAuthority`. It admits each attempt before the secret/PII swap, the hooks and the handler. - A denial is terminal: it never fails over, the embedding queue doesn't retry it, and it isn't retryable when a model call inside an action handler raises it. - The policy sees the model type the caller asked for, before any LLM-mode override. - With no policy installed, behavior is unchanged. - `runActionsByMode` and plugin-assistant plan steps now settle through the action gate (`settleActionHandler`). - Removed, with zero in-repo callers: the `zod-schema.agent-runtime` subpath, `ToolPolicyService` / `getFilteredActions` / `isActionAllowed`, 17 private model wrappers in `runtime.ts`, and duplicate helpers. `canonicalJson` and `parseBooleanFromText` now each have one implementation. The shared canonical backup JSON rejects sparse array holes. ### agent - `ELIZA_PROTECTED_PROFILE=dstack-cpu` (captured from the process env at entry) runs admission before config load, vault hydration, API listen and plugin resolution. - `ELIZA_TEE_*`, `ELIZA_DSTACK_*`, `ELIZA_CONFIDENTIAL_*` and `ELIZA_PROTECTED_*` are env-only. They are blocked from config and API env writes, and the state-dir `config.env` can't apply or persist them either. - Evidence-factory registration is refused under the profile. - Audit sinks are async, and a failure in a required sink now rejects. Retention never deletes audit log types. Confidential-runtime schema is v2. ### cloud - API key create, delete, regenerate and mobile revoke write their audit event in the same transaction. A sink failure rolls the change back. - An oversized client `X-Request-Id` is dropped from the event instead of failing the write. - PII scrub markers record their inspection scope (migration `0506`). - There is a single retryable provider-fallback middleware with a `ProviderFallbackPolicy` hook. A refusal throws `PROVIDER_FALLBACK_REFUSED`. - With `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_REQUIRED`, agent env secrets no longer fall back to plaintext. `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_REQUIRE_AAD` is documented as off until writers pass coordinates. - New `user_consents` table (migration `0507`) with `GET`/`POST /api/v1/me/consents` for `vision_capture`. GET also returns `effective` (the enforced policy, with `basis` and `defaultGranted`) and `capture.modelCallRecording` (the deployment's recording policy). - There's a user-scoped live `POST /api/v1/me/data-export` that requires a recent login. - A single `getRequestIp` helper (`cf-connecting-ip` first) serves all webhooks. Expired `auth_events` are purged. ### app / ui - There is one session-cookie parser: identical duplicate cookies are accepted, conflicting ones rejected. - Logout revokes every presented session credential, including conflicting duplicates, and also expires the `Domain` variant. - Revoking a session closes its open WebSockets (1008). Admission re-reads the session after binding, so a revoke that races the handshake can't leave a socket open. - The privacy panel shows the deployment's model-call recording policy (read-only) and leaves vision/screen capture to device permissions. It uses the live export endpoint. - Removed the dead first-run fork, update policy, `api/response` and `globals` shims. ### Review feedback addressed - Migration collisions: renumbered to `0506_pii_scrub_markers_inspection_scope`, `0507_user_consents` and `0508_app_notification_secret_envelope_v2`. These are the filenames present in the current branch. - The sparse-array bug in canonical backup JSON is fixed. - The consents API exposes the effective policy and default, as distinct from an explicit grant. ### Model-call recording, session controls and attestation **Recording (no consent; off in production):** - The cloud records billed model calls under one policy: `LLM_TRAJECTORY_CAPTURE=on|off`, otherwise off in production and on elsewhere. The `trajectory_training` consent purpose is removed. - Payloads never go to the public `BLOB` bucket. They use a dedicated private store when one is bound, otherwise Postgres. - Bodies are encrypted with row-bound org field encryption. - `LLM_TRAJECTORY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 90) sets retention, enforced by a daily purge. - Account deletion removes payload objects by org prefix, orphans included. - The agent's trajectory gate defaults off under `ELIZA_PROTECTED_PROFILE`. Operators can still enable it inside the TEE. **Session and data safeguards:** - **Automatic logoff:** the protected profile gets a 30-minute idle logoff and a 12h absolute cap. `ELIZA_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES` sets the idle window in any profile. The idle window slides only on real user activity (`x-eliza-last-activity` from the shared UI clients, allowed in CORS for remote agents), never on background polling or sockets. - **Password change:** revokes every other session and closes its sockets. - **Auth store:** row counts no longer assume success. - **Media:** under the protected profile, media is served only after authentication. Same-origin cookie auth keeps ``/`

topPRs.title: fix(core,agent,app): quality-review bug fixes
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
This PR fixes the behavior bugs from the core/agent/app quality review (report §3). It includes only bugs that need **no owner decision** and **do not overlap** the unmerged `shaw/agent-framework-review-refactor-e7a9a1` branch. Each fix is its own commit with a regression test that fails on the old code and passes with the fix.

Dead-code deletion, consolidation, and the 28 owner decisions (D1–D28) are not in this PR. They wait for review.

## Fixes (report bug numbers)
**Security / data loss**
- agent: capability-router persistence refuses to overwrite corrupt state instead of erasing every endpoint and trust policy (#1).
- agent: malformed trust-policy / allowed-modules env settings now fail closed (#2).
- agent: VFS git sends the host GitHub token only to `https://github.com`, and an empty env var counts as unset (#3).
- agent: postgres restore and the VFS `>>` redirect propagate failures instead of swallowing them (#5, #7).
- elizacloud: one shared `config.env` writer with the agent, which removes the lost-update race and applies the denylist and 0700 mode (#8).
- core: cloud log-sink redaction fails closed through the single `log-redaction` walker (#9).
- app scripts: the App Store sandbox audit and the adb install hash check now fail closed (#11, #12).
- desktop: the main-process API bearer is scoped to the local agent origin on reset/disconnect (#37).
- android: the SMS gateway secret is no longer written into the tracked `build.gradle`; the template reads env when Gradle runs (#38).
- app api: first-run rollback always restores config and env (#41).
- CLI: `db reset` uses the runtime's PGlite resolver (#42), and `config show/get` redact secrets in every output mode (#43).

**Functional**
- agent: self-API calls use `resolveSelfApiBaseUrl` instead of a hard-coded 2138 (#13).
- agent: runtime ops settle on throw, and same-family switches get a strategy (#15, #16).
- assistant: `TargetSourceRegistryService` is registered (#17).
- agent: view navigate stops after an invalid body, and `X-ElizaOS-UI-Language` is honored (#18, #28).
- electrobun: no duplicate voice turn, `resetSteward` clears the real state dir, branded builds read `${namespace}.json` (#21–#23).
- core: streaming context is shared across bundle copies (#33); literal NUL bytes removed from `voice-gate.ts` (#34); the reasoning filter covers all 7 canonical tags (#35).
- mobile/embed: repeated warm deep links apply (#46), and embed auth failures are logged (#47).
- app api: a key the user types beats an env key (#49).
- steward: a 409 tenant-exists response now stops with a typed recovery error (#50).
- electrobun: the updater no longer owns the menu dispatcher, and event cursors page forward (#51, #52).
- electrobun: one desktop env-flag parser (#53).
- CLI: honest exit codes for update, doctor and auth; canonical config writes; phantom pool fields dropped (#54, #57).
- app: the browser barrel re-exports ui's canonical `AppWindowRenderer`, and the dead fork is deleted (#56).
- benchmarks: recall-bench and entity-voice-bench import from their plugin homes (#58).
- agent: dead `shouldReject` branch removed from the context inspector (#59).

**Build / release tooling**
- The gateway maintainer deploys only on the explicit drift exit code 3 (#60).
- Device leases are written atomically (#61).
- apk extract failures propagate (#62).
- `sleepSync` is defined (#24).
- `clean-repo` removes homepage outputs (#26).
- The voice catalog fails closed and the default id is `same` (#36).
- The walkthrough, fused-lib, libllama, iOS smoke and patch-deps scripts fail closed (#63, #64, #66–#68).
- The renderer shares the LP3/VPS flag predicates with the native build policy (#65).

## Behavior changes to review
- `resolveActivePgliteDataDir` (agent `runtime/eliza.ts`) is now exported and gives `config.database.pglite.dataDir` precedence over `PGLITE_DATA_DIR`, matching `applyDatabaseConfigToEnv`. This file is also edited on the agent-framework branch, so expect a small merge.
- Desktop flags now honor `on`/`off`/`yes`/`no`. An unrecognized value keeps the default and logs a warning.
- Cloud log redaction output differs slightly. Cycles now show as `[Circular]`, and a PEM block masks to `***`. It masks the same or more than before.
- The benchmarks now import `@elizaos/plugin-assistant` and `@elizaos/plugin-relationships`. These resolve through workspace hoisting and are not yet declared in the suites' `package.json`.

## Verification
- `tsc` passes for core, agent, app (host + renderer), plugin-assistant and plugin-elizacloud.
- Biome reports 0 errors on the 136 changed files.
- All 55 new or changed test files pass under their package runners (vitest, bun test, node --test).
- Each fix was also checked against the pre-fix code, where its regression test fails.
- I have not run the full `bun run verify` locally because the machine is heavily loaded; hosted CI covers it.

topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
## Final integration verification

Combined host-policy head `ebf1940c33d8c528eddf6d59ac5aa2989b705c2d` includes the reviewed presentation race fix. Pinned Bun 1.4.2 / Node 24.15.0 root `bun run verify` passed all 284 tasks and final audits. Independent task HTTP/SQLite suites passed 25 tests; external-credential config and Cloud policy suites passed 2 each. Browser, Google, PDF, Cloud image, UI task/speech and managed Gmail suites all passed. Exact PR-head hosted checks remain a separate merge gate.

## Current validation

Head `ebf1940c33d8c528eddf6d59ac5aa2989b705c2d` includes the post-refresh presentation fence: a pause or authorization change during an awaited refresh suppresses the stale choice. Presentation fixtures use actual HTTP admission, file-backed SQLite, and filesystem effects. Integrated host-policy head `ebf1940c33d8c528eddf6d59ac5aa2989b705c2d` passes 25 task tests, two credential-configuration tests, and two Cloud action-policy tests under Node24.15.0/Bun1.4.2. Its full root verification and exact-head hosted checks are running. Prior combined head22a855 passed all284 tasks and final audits; that earlier result does not qualify the new revision by itself.

## Current review validation

Head `350969b9b913a36eac28e87a41d270fc2ba27289` merges the reviewed dependency stack. External credential persistence tests passed (2), Cloud registration-policy tests passed (2), and both owning typecheck/lint checks passed. Cold imports exceeded the original five-second test timeout; the two full-plugin integration checks now explicitly allow 60 seconds and passed through the standard invocation. No assertions were removed. Combined-stack root verification is running at this exact head; hosted checks are pending. Linked original-head artifacts were not regenerated.

# Relates to

Depends on #32976, #32980, #32981, #32983, #32984 and #32985. This branch includes that stack and must not merge ahead of its dependencies.

# Change

Hosts that hydrate credentials from a protected store can select environment values that saveElizaConfig omits from serialized config while preserving in-memory settings. Hosts can also disable Cloud account-action registration while retaining inference models, providers and services. Defaults preserve existing behavior; malformed host policies fail explicitly.

These generic controls replace product-named consumer patches. Exact-value omission does not scrub previous files, logs, transformed values or other stores. Hosts retain migration and credential custody. Action registration policy does not authorize arbitrary SDK calls.

# Original-head validation

- Two actual config filesystem tests passed: external secret omission, ordinary persistence, input preservation, mode 0600, repeated save, default behavior and invalid-policy write preservation.
- Two assembled Cloud plugin tests passed: actions absent with inference/providers retained, default actions and invalid policy rejection.
- Owning typecheck/lint/dependency builds: 78 tasks passed.
- Root bun run verify: 284 tasks and repository audits passed.

## Known gaps

topPRs.title: feat: persist host-issued task choices for authenticated presentation
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
## Final integration verification

Combined host-policy head `ebf1940c33d8c528eddf6d59ac5aa2989b705c2d` includes the reviewed presentation race fix. Pinned Bun 1.4.2 / Node 24.15.0 root `bun run verify` passed all 284 tasks and final audits. Independent task HTTP/SQLite suites passed 25 tests; external-credential config and Cloud policy suites passed 2 each. Browser, Google, PDF, Cloud image, UI task/speech and managed Gmail suites all passed. Exact PR-head hosted checks remain a separate merge gate.

## Current validation

Head `fbb16af0dbdc8457bd323ced1589b832bc2f7665` includes the post-refresh presentation fence: a pause or authorization change during an awaited refresh suppresses the stale choice. Presentation fixtures use actual HTTP admission, file-backed SQLite, and filesystem effects. Integrated host-policy head `ebf1940c33d8c528eddf6d59ac5aa2989b705c2d` passes 25 task tests, two credential-configuration tests, and two Cloud action-policy tests under Node24.15.0/Bun1.4.2. Its full root verification and exact-head hosted checks are running. Prior combined head22a855 passed all284 tasks and final audits; that earlier result does not qualify the new revision by itself.

## Current repair and validation

Head `fbb16af0dbdc8457bd323ced1589b832bc2f7665` integrates develop, including the reminder context change. A real HTTP/Pause regression reproduced stale choice delivery after refresh. Reads now recheck the task epoch, active status and authorization immediately before returning the widget.

All 21 related HTTP, presentation and choice tests pass. The new presentation scenarios now use authenticated HTTP task admission, file-backed SQLite and actual filesystem selection effects; they preserve restart, stale publication, forged labels and actor isolation checks. Agent typecheck initially failed because a cold ignore-scripts install had no embeddings declarations; the owning builds and final typecheck/lint are running. Full combined-stack verification and current-head hosted checks remain required. Earlier-head results below are historical and do not qualify this head.

# Relates to

Depends on #32976, #32980, #32981, #32983 and #32984. This branch includes the preceding stack and must not merge ahead of its dependencies.

# Change

Chat delivery needs a durable view of a host-issued task choice without offering it again or executing a task. Add SqliteTaskPresentation over existing choice authority: reads refresh commitment state, expired/paused/old-epoch offers disappear, and a stored generation fences late publication after replacement or Clear. Capture option input before asynchronous storage so later caller mutation cannot change the response schema. Add public service exports for presentation, choices and their SQLite authority store.

Hosts retain authenticated route binding, product UI and effect policy. Models and renderer payloads cannot publish authoritative offers through this service.

# Original-head validation

- 16 focused SQLite/task-choice tests passed, including real disk close/reopen, paused restart, actor isolation, expiry, forged labels, mutable input, concurrent replacement, Clear races, and malformed storage.
- Owning typecheck/lint and dependency builds passed 76 tasks.
- Root verification passed all 284 tasks and repository audits.

# Evidence Gate

<!-- evidence-row:llm-trajectory -->

# Evidence Details

SQLite tests exercise real persistence and task authority with a controlled actuator. They do not establish authenticated product chat delivery. Inherited UI screenshots/video/OCR, when attached, are from unchanged TaskChoice at #32981 (`a712e7d27c8506a31f2ebc70336234c1535be6cc`), and demonstrate that dependency only.

## Known gaps

The initial resume test incorrectly called the synchronous control API; it was corrected to resume through a fresh runtime observation. Root verification passed; hosted CI/review remain pending. Product chat wiring and consumer adoption are separate work; no live Google, Chromium, device or user acceptance is claimed. Clear removes presentation only and does not replace explicit task cancellation or revoke an effect already committed by the authority.
